While ___ happens in one myth, ___ happens in the other. Both heroes show ___ because ___. Use a paragraph from a student draft with permission, or a teacher sample."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"teach","text":"Reteach: Strong essays vary sentences with appositives, prepositional phrases and subordinating clauses, keep a formal style and consistent tense, and use transitions such as similarly, in contrast and as a result. Revising also means checking commas, proper nouns and agreement."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Guided Practice: Look at this sentence: Percy is a hero. He is brave. He saves his friends. How could you combine and vary it?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"Percy, a young demigod, proves his bravery when he saves his friends. The appositive adds detail and the sentences sound smoother."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Which words in this sentence are too casual, and what could replace them? 'The myths are kind of the same because the heroes do a bunch of cool stuff.'"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"Kind of, a bunch and cool stuff are casual. I could write: The myths are similar because the heroes perform remarkable deeds."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Quick Check: Revise two sentences from your own essay. Vary the pattern, keep the tone formal, and add one transition."},{"type":"eld-panel","purpose":"Support English learners in revising sentences for variety, formality and cohesion.","sayAsk":"Frames: I varied the sentence by adding ___. A more formal way to say that is ___. I added the transition ___ to show ___. Say: You said 'it sounds bad' - we can say: 'The sentences are repetitive.'","watchFor":"If student changes only one word, then ask: Did the sentence pattern change? If student's revision is a run-on, then have them read it aloud and find where the idea ends. Success: revision keeps meaning and sounds formal."},{"type":"support-table","rows":[{"situation":"Struggling with: sentence variety","tryThis":"Offer starters: By ___, the hero... or After ___, the hero... and let students say the sentence aloud first."},{"situation":"Ready for extension","tryThis":"Ask students to find a nonrestrictive element in their draft and check its commas, then combine formal tone with varied sentences in one paragraph."}]}]},{"id":"huddle-3-seminar-and-podcast","title":"Huddle 3: Claim, Evidence and Paraphrasing for Speaking","minutes":13,"standards":[],"routine":"Huddle","blocks":[{"type":"paragraph","audience":"teacher","text":"Pull students who need support stating a claim and strongest evidence aloud, paraphrasing a peer, or connecting myths to modern values. When a peer speaks, paraphrase by restating the idea in your own words before you add yours."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Guided Practice: What is one claim you made in your essay, and what is your strongest evidence?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"My claim is that both myths teach loyalty. Partner B paraphrases using: What I hear you saying is..."},{"type":"eld-panel","purpose":"Give English learners structured language for speaking and paraphrasing.","sayAsk":"Frames: My claim is ___. The strongest evidence is ___. This connects to today because ___. What I hear you saying is ___. Say: You said 'she say loyal' - we can say: 'She claims that loyalty is the shared theme.'","watchFor":"If student retells the plot, then ask: What is your claim about the lesson?
